properties.name: Jos Plateau
properties.summary: Volcanic highland in central Nigeria with a cooler climate and tin-mining history.
properties.description: The Jos Plateau is a granite and volcanic upland rising sharply above the surrounding plains. Tin and columbite mining shaped 20th-century Jos. The height brings lower temperatures, Irish potatoes and vegetables, and tourism. Gully erosion is a modern hazard.
properties.character: Inselbergs, temperate crops, mining scars, tourism.
properties.economy: Tourism, remnant mining, highland farming, Jos urban services.
properties.agriculture: Young volcanic and loamy soils with good structure. Cooler temperatures allow temperate vegetables that do not thrive in the lowlands. Mine-pond water is used for small-scale irrigation.
properties.crops: ["Irish potato (Solanum tuberosum) — the premier highland tuber (Bokkos, Mangu belts)","Carrot, cabbage, lettuce, and onion — irrigated vegetable clusters supplying Jos markets","Tomato — both rainfed and irrigation (Jos tomato-processing belt)","Cucumber, green pepper, and garden egg — salad vegetables for urban centres","Apple (Malus domestica) and strawberry — experimental and small-scale orchards","Wheat — small highland plots where night temperatures drop","Maize and beans — lower slopes and deeper valley soils","Coffee (Coffea arabica) — historic plantations around Vom, Barikin Ladi","Tea (Camellia sinensis) — experimental plantings on the cooler margins","Avocado pear — orchards expanding around Jos and Rayfield","Pineapple — mid-altitude sheltered valleys","Eucalyptus, pine, and cypress — planted woodlots for fuelwood and poles"]
properties.planting: ["Plant Irish potato tubers October–November (short rains) and March–April for the main crop","Use raised seedbeds in gully-prone areas to control erosion","Rotate vegetables with leguminous green manures (crotalaria, mucuna) to maintain soil organic matter","Irrigate leafy greens through the dry season using shallow mine ponds and hand-dug wells","Plant windbreak trees (Eucalyptus, Casuarina) on exposed plateau edges to reduce wind damage"]
properties.highlights: ["Coolest large highland in Nigeria","Tin heritage","Shere Hills"]

properties.name: Mambilla Plateau
properties.summary: Nigeria's highest inhabited plateau on the Cameroon border in Taraba.
properties.description: Mambilla is a grassland plateau with tea estates and a proposed mega hydropower project. Chappal Waddi (Gangirwal) in the Gashaka-Gumti / border highlands is often cited as Nigeria's highest peak. Access is via steep escarpment roads.
properties.character: Tea, cattle, montane grassland, cloud forest fragments.
properties.economy: Tea, livestock, proposed hydropower, limited tourism.
properties.agriculture: High-altitude andosols and deep loams on ancient volcanic formations. Frosts occur on the highest ground in dry season; rainfall is heavy April–October with persistent cloud cover.
properties.crops: ["Tea (Camellia sinensis) — Ngel Nyaki and other estates, producing black tea for Nigerian market","Arabica coffee (Coffea arabica) — higher-altitude coffee gardens","Potatoes and sweet potatoes — cool-climate tuber staples","Cabbage, carrot, garlic, and leek — highland vegetables for southern markets","Wheat (Triticum aestivum) — smallholder plots on the plateau surface","Apples, pear, and plum — experimental high-altitude deciduous fruits","Fodder grasses and alfalfa for the large cattle herds","Maize and beans — lower escarpment terraces","Medicinal herbs and aromatic plants of the montane grassland","Yam and cocoyam — in sheltered escarpment valleys","Banana and plantain — lower escarpment roadsides","Pinus and Cupressus plantation woodlots for timber and erosion control"]
properties.planting: ["Tea bushes planted on contour terraces at 1,500 m+; plucked year-round in the wet phase","Wheat sown October–November at first break of rains and harvested March–April","Potato seed tubers planted August–September at start of short rains in the montane zone","Contour grass strips and bench terraces essential on steeper ground to halt sheet erosion","Cattle should be excluded from young forest regeneration areas to protect water catchments"]

properties.name: Niger Delta
properties.summary: Africa's largest wetland delta where the Niger meets the Atlantic; Nigeria's petroleum heartland.
properties.description: The delta covers ~70,000 km² of mangrove, freshwater swamp, and barrier islands. It holds the bulk of Nigeria's oil and gas, a dense creek network, and highly politicised environmental and federal-revenue issues.
properties.elevationNote: Mostly near sea level; tidal mangrove
properties.character: Mangrove, oilfields, riverine settlements, barrier islands.
properties.economy: Oil and gas, fisheries, boat transport, refining.
properties.agriculture: Hydromorphic gleysols, peat, and alluvial deposits on a landscape of seasonally flooded flats, backswamps, and levees. Oil-palm agroforest dominates the better-drained levee ridges; fisheries are economically vital.
properties.crops: ["Oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) — the delta is the heart of Nigeria's smallholder oil-palm belt; red palm oil and kernel extraction","Rubber (Hevea brasiliensis) — plantation and smallholder rubber on drier ridges (Edo, Delta)","Plantain and banana (Musa spp.) — staple carbohydrate on levee soils","Cassava — garri, lafun, and fufu processing across the delta hinterland","Yam — white and yellow yam in the drier northern delta fringe","Rice — both lowland swamp rice and fadama irrigation (Rivers, Delta State paddies)","Cocoyam (Colocasia & Xanthosoma) — shade-tolerant tuber under palm canopy","Fluted pumpkin (Telfairia occidentalis) — ugu leaf vegetable widely intercropped","Vegetables: amaranth, okra, peppers, garden egg — backyard and creek bank gardens","Coconut palm — barrier beaches and island fringes of the delta mouth","Mangrove (Rhizophora, Avicennia) — fuelwood, poles, and fisheries habitat","Fish, shrimp, and crab artisanal fisheries — the delta is Nigeria's richest inland/coastal fishery"]
properties.planting: ["Plant cassava and yam on levee ridges (higher drained ground) away from deep backswamps","Oil palms are usually retained on family farms — propagate by seedling and suckers at 9×9 m spacing","Use mounds and raised beds for vegetables in perennially waterlogged backswamp soils","Construct small fish ponds (earthen ponds) in abandoned rice fields for tilapia and catfish","Avoid draining mangrove wetlands — nursery habitat for fish stocks and shoreline protection"]

properties.name: Guinea Savanna
properties.summary: Wooded savanna belt between southern rainforest and northern Sudan/Sahel savanna.
properties.description: Guinea savanna (southern and northern Guinea) is Nigeria's broad middle belt: shea, yam, sorghum, and cattle routes. Rainfall is typically 900–1,500 mm. It includes much of Kwara, Niger, Kogi, Benue, Nasarawa, and parts of Kaduna and FCT.
properties.character: Parkland trees, seasonal burn, mixed farming.
properties.economy: Yam, shea, grains, livestock corridors, Abuja hinterland.
properties.agriculture: Deep ferric luvisols support root crops and cereals. Shea parklands are retained on farm fields across the belt. Short fallow rotations are common.
properties.crops: ["Yam (Dioscorea rotundata) — white guinea yam is the staple tuber crop","Cassava (Manihot esculenta) — processed into garri, fufu, and flour","Guinea corn / Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) — guinea-corn for ogi, pap, and tuwo","Millet (Pennisetum glaucum) — early-maturing dry-season staple","Maize (Zea mays) — grown as second crop in yam/cassava rotations","Rice (Oryza sativa & O. glaberrima) — lowland fadama and upland varieties","Shea nut (Vitellaria paradoxa) — shea butter extraction, parkland agroforestry","Groundnut / Peanut (Arachis hypogaea) — oilseed and snack crop","Soybean (Glycine max) — expanding for oil and poultry feed","Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) — beans and leaves as vegetable","Sesame (Sesamum indicum) — northern guinea fringe for oilseeds","Mango, citrus, and cashew — scattered commercial orchards"]
properties.planting: ["Plant yam mounds (heaps) with stakes from November–December; seed yam setts planted February–April","Sorghum and millet sown at first rains (April–May); late maize July–August","Cassava stem cuttings planted March–May, harvested 9–18 months later","Shea trees retained as permanent parkland — do not clear mature shea on new farms","Use minimum tillage and tied ridges to reduce runoff on sloping ground"]

properties.name: Idanre Hills
properties.summary: Dramatic granite inselberg cluster and UNESCO-adjacent cultural landscape in Ondo State.
properties.description: Idanre Hills rise abruptly above the Ondo plain with steep ascents, ancient Oke-Idanre settlement ruins, and panoramic views. The hills are a major tourism and pilgrimage destination in southwestern Nigeria.
properties.character: Granite domes, sacred groves, heritage settlement.
properties.economy: Tourism, cocoa hinterland farming.

properties.name: Shere Hills
properties.summary: Rocky highland within the Jos Plateau and a popular hiking destination.
properties.description: Shere Hills form a jagged granite skyline near Jos with peaks including Peak 1 (~1,829 m). Rock climbing, hiking, and cool-climate tourism draw visitors from across Nigeria.
properties.character: Granite tors, hiking trails, cool climate.
properties.economy: Tourism, Jos weekend recreation.

properties.name: Udi–Nsukka Escarpment
properties.summary: Eastern Nigeria escarpment above the Cross River basin; Enugu coal belt.
properties.description: The Udi Hills and Nsukka escarpment mark the edge of the Enugu Plateau. Coal seams here fuelled Nigeria's railway era. The ridge now hosts Enugu city, universities, and forest patches.
properties.character: Coal measures, forest patches, university towns.
properties.economy: Coal heritage, Enugu urban economy, education.

properties.name: Oban Hills
properties.summary: Cross River rainforest highlands linked to the Oban sector of Cross River National Park.
properties.description: Oban Hills lie in the Cross River–Cameroon biodiversity hotspot with lowland and montane rainforest, drill monkeys, and forest elephants (rare). Terrain is rugged and heavily forested.
properties.character: Rainforest, biodiversity hotspot, protected areas.
properties.economy: Ecotourism, conservation, limited hill farming.
properties.agriculture: Acrisols and ferralsols on steep slopes — highly leached but suitable for tree crops. Land-use pressure is intense outside the park boundary with shifting cultivation and cocoa farms.
properties.crops: ["Cocoa (Theobroma cacao) — shaded cocoa agroforestry on park buffer-zone farms","Oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) — semi-wild stands and plantation palms","Rubber (Hevea brasiliensis) — smallholder rubber on gentler slopes","Plantain and banana — staple food of the Efik and Ejagham communities","Cassava and yam — shifting-cultivation staples in the wider district","Cocoyam, sweet potato, and taro — under-storey root crops","Okra, pepper, and amaranth — backyard vegetables in the villages","Citrus (oranges, tangerine, lime) — expanding market-garden orchards","Kolanut (Cola nitida & acuminata) — traditional cash crop with ceremonial uses","Bush mango (Irvingia gabonensis) — ogbono soup seeds from retained forest trees","Raffia palm (Raphia spp.) — palm wine, thatch, and raffia fibre","Timber species: mahogany, obeche, iroko — strictly protected inside the national park"]
properties.planting: ["Practice agroforestry: retain large native forest trees when planting cocoa — they shade the crop and protect watersheds","Build contour stone lines or grass barriers on hillsides to stop sheet erosion","Rotate cocoa farms with 10–15 year fallows under secondary forest to rebuild soil organic matter","Plant multi-purpose nitrogen-fixing trees (Gliricidia, Albizia) along farm boundaries","Respect park boundaries — avoid clearing new farms inside Cross River National Park"]

properties.name: Aso Rock
properties.summary: Iconic granite inselberg dominating Abuja's skyline and the Presidential Villa.
properties.description: Aso Rock is a 400-metre monolith at the heart of the Federal Capital Territory. It gives its name to Aso Villa (Presidential residence) and is visible across Abuja's Central Area.
properties.elevationNote: ~936 m summit; ~400 m relief above plain
properties.character: Granite monolith, seat of government backdrop.

properties.name: Zuma Rock
properties.summary: Massive monolith on the Abuja–Kaduna corridor, nicknamed the Gateway to Abuja.
properties.description: Zuma Rock rises ~725 m above the surrounding plain near Madalla in Niger State. Its distinctive face is visible from the Abuja–Kaduna expressway and features in Nigerian iconography.
properties.elevationNote: ~725 m above surrounding plain (~1,125 m AMSL)
properties.character: Granite inselberg, expressway landmark.
properties.highlights: ["Gateway to Abuja","725 m monolith","Niger–FCT border landmark"]

properties.name: Olumo Rock
properties.summary: Historic Egba refuge rock in Abeokuta, Ogun State.
properties.description: Olumo Rock served as a natural fortress during 19th-century inter-tribal wars. Today it is a major cultural tourism site with caves, carvings, and views over Abeokuta.
properties.character: Granite refuge, cultural tourism.

properties.name: Chappal Waddi (Gangirwal)
properties.summary: Nigeria's highest point (~2,419 m) on the Mambilla / Gashaka border highlands.
properties.description: Chappal Waddi (also Gangirwal) lies in the Gashaka-Gumti / Mambilla border highlands in Taraba State. The peak is often cited as Nigeria's highest ground, in montane grassland and forest ecotone.
properties.character: Montane grassland, border highlands, cloud forest fringe.

properties.name: Wadi Kuru Peak
properties.summary: Notable peak on the Jos Plateau used for mountaineering practice.
properties.description: Wadi Kuru is among the recognised high points on the Jos Plateau near Jos city, popular with hikers and mountaineering clubs.
properties.character: Granite highland, hiking.

properties.name: Obudu Plateau
properties.summary: Cool montane plateau and ranch resort in the Cross River highlands.
properties.description: Obudu Plateau rises above the Cross River lowlands with grassland, ranch tourism, and a cable car. It is among Nigeria's best-known highland holiday destinations outside Jos and Mambilla.
properties.character: Montane grassland, ranch tourism, cloud forest fringe.
properties.economy: Tourism, ranching, hospitality.
properties.agriculture: Acidic montane loams over basement rocks with high rainfall. The plateau supports high-value cool-season vegetables and ranching, but steep slopes need careful erosion control.
properties.crops: ["Irish potato (Solanum tuberosum) — highland potato supply to Calabar and eastern markets","Carrot, cabbage, cauliflower, and broccoli — premium out-of-season vegetables","Garlic and onion bulbs — high-altitude bulb crops with long storage","Apple, pear, and peach orchards — established at the cattle ranch and community plots","Tea and coffee — experimental plantations leveraging the cool climate","Wheat and oats — small highland grain plots","Beans and peas — cool-season legumes for soil rotation","Pasture grasses (Cenchrus, Pennisetum, Brachiaria) — ranch fodder and hay","Medicinal herbs and honey production — montane agroforestry niches","Tomato and pepper — irrigated dry-season gardens","Plantain and banana — in sheltered, lower escarpment positions","Pine, cypress, and eucalyptus woodlots for timber and watershed protection"]
properties.planting: ["Sow potato tubers May–June as rains establish; harvest December–January at the Obudu altitude","Ranch cattle should be rotationally grazed to avoid soil compaction and slope erosion","Build stone-walled terraces and contour hedgerows on all sloping fields to halt sheet wash","Dry-season vegetables require reliable water — harvest into the cooler cloud-forest dew zone","Retain riparian forest strips along streams to feed the Obudu water-catchment areas"]
